title: Reactive Forms
summary: Define the form model in TypeScript — powerful for bigger, dynamic forms.
heading: Reactive Forms

blocks.text: Reactive forms flip things around: instead of the template owning the form, you build the form model in TypeScript. That makes the form easy to read, test, and change at runtime — ideal for larger or dynamic forms.
A FormControl is a single field. A FormGroup bundles controls into one form. You create them in the class, then connect them in the template.

blocks.label: signup.ts
signup.html
blocks.code:
<form [formGroup]="form" (ngSubmit)="submit()">
  <input formControlName="name" placeholder="Name">
  <input formControlName="email" placeholder="Email">
  <button type="submit">Sign up</button>
</form>

blocks.text: Pass validators when you create each control. They live in the class, not the template.

blocks.label: signup.ts

blocks.text: Read a control's state to show messages and control the submit button:

blocks.label: signup.html
blocks.code:
<input formControlName="name">
@if (form.controls.name.invalid && form.controls.name.touched) {
  <small>Name needs at least 3 characters.</small>
}

<button [disabled]="form.invalid">Sign up</button>

blocks.text: Writing new FormControl everywhere gets repetitive. FormBuilder (injected with inject) builds the same form with less code.

blocks.label: signup.ts

blocks.text: Because the model lives in code, you can watch any value change as the user types — useful for live search, dependent fields, or autosave.
A FormGroup can hold another FormGroup — perfect for grouping related fields like an address.

blocks.label: signup.ts

blocks.text: Pass a nested FormGroup down to a child component as an input. The child binds it with [formGroup] — the parent still owns the whole form.

blocks.text: A FormArray holds a changing number of controls — like a list of phone numbers the user can add to or remove.

items: Reactive forms define the model in the class; import ReactiveFormsModule.
FormBuilder (fb.group) is a shorter way to build the form.
valueChanges lets you react as values change.
Best for large, dynamic, or heavily-validated forms.
